content:
The test image shows a **stem junction** covered in dense, dark gray-black fungal mass with some white patches visible. Key features: dark/almost black fungal growth at a node, grayish dusty texture, and possible white mycelium underneath.

Top stem candidates: Gray_Mold, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Anthracnose, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.

Viewing one reference from each of 8 classes:

The Gray_Mold/stem/Bugwood_23 reference (ID 1573933) is visually very similar to the test image - both show brown/dark fungal growth at a stem junction. The test image has darker/more advanced sporulation but same location pattern.

Final view - Anthracnose stem to cover another class:

**Summary of evidence:**

- **Test image**: Stem junction/node with dense dark gray-black fungal mass, dusty/granular texture, white patches visible within the dark growth
- **Gray_Mold/stem/Bugwood_23** (ID 1573933): Most visually similar — shows brown/dark fungal lesion at a stem junction in the same image style; test image represents more advanced sporulation stage
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots/stem**: Lighter, fluffier grayish mycelium — less dark than test
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/stem**: White mycelium at soil line — doesn't match
- **Southern_Blight/stem**: Bleached/brown stem tissue — doesn't match the fungal mass
- **Anthracnose/stem**: Microscopic acervuli on orange tissue — doesn't match
- **Alternaria** references: All microscopic spore images — couldn't compare macroscopically
- **Gray_Mold** description matches: dense velvety gray-brown spore mass on stems, stem junction lesions that girdle the stem

The dark compact fungal mass at the stem node, with grayish dusty spore texture and some white mycelial patches, is most consistent with Gray Mold (Botrytis) heavy sporulation, and the Gray_Mold/stem/Bugwood_23 reference is the closest macroscopic match found.
